layman_headline: Solana trade is working — up 4% — but the broader market just hit a speed bump.
layman_explanation: Our Solana position is up about 4% from where we bought it, heading toward our 15% profit target. The broader market pulled back today after the Fed chair signaled inflation is still a concern, dragging Bitcoin down nearly 3%. The swing trade candidates this cycle are either stablecoins (no trade opportunity), already-extended movers, or new tokens with no technical data to analyze. There's no compelling new entry right now.
layman_action: Hold the Solana position and let it work toward the $115 target. The stop-loss at $92 protects downside. Don't chase anything new until a clearer setup emerges.
expert_reasoning: The current swing candidates are poor quality: MON is in a downtrend (-6.7% 7d, -46% from ATH), PUMP and LIT are already extended after 13-18% weekly rallies with no technical confirmation data, and the rest are stablecoins. SOL remains the best exposure — it has high liquidity ($6.2B volume), a clear trend, and our entry at $101 gives us buffer above the $92 stop. BTC dominance at 59% is suppressing altcoin performance broadly, and Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole stance adds macro risk that makes adding new positions inadvisable. The Greed reading at 73 also counsels patience rather than chasing.
risk_factors: Fed hawkishness could trigger a broader risk-off move, pushing BTC below $76K support and dragging SOL down
BTC dominance at 59% continues to siphon capital away from altcoins, limiting SOL upside
SOL's 14.7% weekly gain may be extended — a pullback to $98-100 is possible before continuation
watch_list: SOL price action near $108-110 resistance — a break above could accelerate toward $115 target
BTC reaction at $76,000 support — a break below would likely invalidate the SOL trade
Follow-up Fed commentary and market reaction over the weekend to gauge macro risk
market_context: BTC pulled back 2.8% to $78.3K after Fed Chair Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole remarks, but is still up 1.4% on the week. Fear & Greed at 73 (Greed) suggests decent sentiment but caution against aggressive new entries.
context_banner: Existing SOL position is performing well at +4%; no new high-conviction setups warrant capital deployment in this pullback environment.

key_signals.description: Greed at 73 and rising — decent sentiment but approaching levels where new entries carry elevated reversal risk.
Bitcoin dipped to $78.4K as Fed's Warsh downplayed softer inflation prints, creating near-term macro headwind for risk assets.
BlackRock pulled in 115% of all BTC ETF inflows in one day — institutional demand remains concentrated and supportive of BTC floor.
SOL volume at $6.2B remains elevated, supporting the continuation thesis toward $115 as long as $98 support holds.
Bitcoin outperforming stocks and correlating with gold — macro narrative supports crypto as a hedge, but BTC dominance at 59% limits alt upside.
